title: DevEx Docs Operating Procedures: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Canonical Fixes
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This page defines the operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API example snippets, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes list for top support issues. The intent is to create a repeatable, reviewable process that keeps examples accurate, minimizes developer friction, and reduces support load through clear, discoverable documentation.

Scope

- SDK guides (Python, Node, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and templates (repo templates, minimal apps, example integration patterns)
- API examples (curl, REST, SDK usage, streaming, tool-calls)
- Docs-site operating procedures (publishing, versioning, redirects, telemetry)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (triaged, tested, and documented solutions)

Principles

1. Keep examples runnable: all code blocks must be copy-paste runnable or include an upfront note describing required environment/credentials.
2. Single source of truth: canonical examples live in the docs repo and are referenced by quickstarts and SDK repos.
3. Small, focused examples: prefer 10-30 lines that demonstrate a single pattern.
4. Test coverage: examples are covered by CI smoke checks and quickstart end-to-end tests where feasible.
5. Ownership and cadence: every doc has an owner, reviewers, and a review cadence (quarterly).

Ownership and Roles

- Doc owner: responsible for accuracy, triage of issues, and quarterly review.
- Maintainers: SDK engineers who update samples when APIs change.
- DevEx lead: ensures CI, release, and site pipelines are healthy.
- Support liaison: tracks top issues and ensures canonical fixes are published.

Canonical Metadata (required fields for all DevEx docs)

- title (string)
- summary (short paragraph)
- author (name)
- owner_team (engineering | product | customer-success)
- status (draft | in_review | published)
- created_at (YYYY-MM-DD)
- last_updated (YYYY-MM-DD)
- reviewers (list of names)
- labels (0-8 short tags)
- related_pages (list of internal links)
- confidentiality (internal | restricted)

Operating Procedures: Authoring and Publishing

1) Create draft in docs repo
   - New docs MUST start as a markdown file in the docs repository (docs/devex/...). Use the standard template: header metadata frontmatter and a short summary.
   - Template header example:

```yaml
---
title: "Quickstart: Text Generation (Python)"
summary: "Minimal app showing text generation with streaming responses."
author: "Ava Martinez"
owners: ["eng-developer-experience"]
status: draft
created_at: 2025-09-15
last_updated: 2025-09-15
labels: ["quickstart","sdk","python"]
---
```

2) Local verification
   - Run linting: docs-lint (checks headings, code fence languages, link formatting).
   - Run example smoke test: the repo has a test harness (docs/tests/run_example.sh) that executes quickstart examples against a staging key. If examples require paid resources, mark them as 'manual test required' in the metadata.

3) Pull request process
   - Open a PR into main/docs with the change. Include :
     - What changed and why
     - Links to related SDK or API changes
     - Test run output (CI link)
   - Include at least one reviewer from SDK maintainers and one from DevEx. Use the label 'docs-change' on the PR.

4) Merge and publish
   - On merge, the docs CI will build and deploy to staging. The DevEx lead must verify the staging build within 48 hours.
   - After verification, the PR author or owner may promote to production release by merging the release PR to the site branch. Production deploys happen during the site deploy window (Mon-Fri 02:00-04:00 UTC).

Docs-site Operating Procedures

- Versioning
  - Docs are versioned by SDK major releases (e.g., python v1.x, v2.x). Use the path /sdk/python/v{major}/quickstart for versioned content.
  - Deprecated endpoints and examples should include a deprecation banner with timeline and recommended migration.

- Redirects
  - When moving or renaming pages, add a redirect entry in docs/redirects.yaml. Keep redirects in place for at least 12 months.

- Telemetry and broken-links
  - Configure the site to run weekly broken-link checks. Failures create a ticket in the devex-docs JIRA board.
  - Capture click telemetry for quickstarts and API examples to prioritize improvements (telemetry ID in page metadata).

- Accessibility
  - All code samples must include language annotations and keyboard-accessible copy controls. Alt text required for all images.

Testing and CI

- Example smoke tests
  - docs/tests/run_example.sh --example=python-quickstart-text-gen --api_key=STAGING_KEY
  - CI executes minimal operations: auth, a small gen request (max_tokens=16), and response schema validate.

- End-to-end quickstart tests (weekly)
  - Full quickstarts are run weekly in a scheduled pipeline. Failures are triaged by devex on-call.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (Process)

1) Triage incoming issues: Support tags docs-related tickets with component 'docs' and severity.
2) Reproduce and create minimal failing example.
3) Assign to doc owner and add to quarterly documentation backlog if not high priority.
4) Publish canonical fix: solution must include root cause, one-line fix, code snippet, and test notes.

Canonical Fix Template (include in each canonical fix doc)

- Title
- Symptom (what users see)
- Root cause
- Fix (1-3 steps)
- Code snippet showing corrected usage
- Tests performed and CI links
- Related pages and SDK PRs

Example canonical fix (authentication failure with streaming)

- Symptom: Streaming examples return 401 with message 'invalid API key' when run with staging key stored as plain text.
- Root cause: New auth middleware rejects requests without the 'X-Client-Version' header when key is from older staging pools.
- Fix:
  1. Update example to set header: headers={"X-Client-Version": "devex-e2e/2025-10-12"}
  2. Regenerate example and run smoke test.

Code snippet (Python):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"), headers={"X-Client-Version": "devex-e2e/2025-10-12"})
resp = client.text.generate("Write a haiku about GPUs", max_tokens=16)
print(resp.text)
```

Monitoring doc health and KPIs

- Key metrics (tracked monthly):
  - Example test pass rate (goal: >= 98%)
  - Time to update after API change (goal: < 7 days for critical changes)
  - Top-5 docs by unique views (to prioritize improvements)
  - Support tickets linked to docs (goal: reduce by 30% YoY)

Quarterly Review Checklist (owner-run)

1. Run smoke test suite and record results.
2. Review telemetry and top-viewed pages.
3. Validate code snippets against latest SDK release.
4. Confirm redirects and versioned pages are still valid.
5. Update last_updated metadata and notify reviewers.

Appendix: Example workflow for a new Python quickstart

1. Author creates docs/devex/quickstarts/python/text-gen-quickstart.md using the quickstart template.
2. Add smoke test under docs/tests/examples/python-text-gen.test.sh.
3. Open PR with 'docs-change' label, request reviews from @python-sdk and @devex.
4. On approval, merge to main/docs. CI deploys to staging; verify artifacts and run smoke tests.
5. Promote to production during the next deploy window.
